record.paper_title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)
record.original_question: How many ultratypes of L_infty-spaces are there? Two Banach spaces X and Y have the same ultratype, or are ultra-isomorphic, when there is an ultrafilter U such that the ultrapowers X_U and Y_U are isomorphic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X and Y be (real or complex) Banach spaces. For an ultrafilter U on an index set I, denote by X_U the Banach space ultrapower of X with respect to U, defined as the quotient ℓ_∞(I,X)/N_U where N_U = {(x_i) : lim_{i→U} ‖x_i‖ = 0}, equipped with the quotient norm. Say that X and Y have the same ultratype (or are ultra-isomorphic) if there exists an ultrafilter U such that X_U and Y_U are isomorphic as Banach spaces. This defines an equivalence relation on the class of Banach spaces.

Recall that, for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and λ ≥ 1, a Banach space X is an L_{p,λ}-space if every finite-dimensional subspace of X is contained in a finite-dimensional subspace F of X with Banach–Mazur distance d(F, ℓ_p^{dim F}) ≤ λ. A Banach space is an L_p-space if it is an L_{p,λ}-space for some λ ≥ 1.

Determine the cardinality of the set of equivalence classes, under the relation of having the same ultratype, of the class of L_∞-spaces. That is: how many distinct ultratypes of L_∞-spaces are there?
artifact.status_search_result: Work on ultrapowers of L_∞-spaces has identified at least two distinct ultratypes among separable L_∞-spaces (that of the C(K)-spaces and that of the Gurariĭ space), and has produced further partial structural results, but the precise number (in particular whether there are only finitely many, countably many, or a continuum of ultratypes of L_∞-spaces) does not appear to have been determined in the literature. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On ultrapowers of Banach spaces of type L_∞
status_evidence.snippet: Studies ultratypes of L_∞-spaces, showing C(K)-spaces and the Gurariĭ space give different ultratypes and producing partial classification results.
status_evidence.claim: Distinct ultratypes among L_∞-spaces have been exhibited but no full count of ultratypes is given.

status_evidence.title: On ultrapowers of Banach spaces of type L_∞ (ResearchGate)
status_evidence.snippet: All M-spaces have ultrapowers isomorphic to ultrapowers of c_0; no ultrapower of the Gurariĭ space is complemented in any M-space.
status_evidence.claim: At least two ultratypes of L_∞-spaces are known, but the total number is not determined.
